title: Routine C4d immunohistochemistry in cardiac allografts: Long-term outcomes
venue: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
study_context: Prospective C4d staining of 5840 endomyocardial biopsies from 296 heart-transplant recipients, with clinical follow-up and autopsy evaluation in a deceased subset.
population_or_data: Prospective C4d staining of 5840 endomyocardial biopsies from 296 heart-transplant recipients, with clinical follow-up and autopsy evaluation in a deceased subset.
task: Prospective C4d staining of 5840 endomyocardial biopsies from 296 heart-transplant recipients, with clinical follow-up and autopsy evaluation in a deceased subset.
method: Correlation of biopsy C4d immunoreactivity with cardiac dysfunction, HLA status, CAV and death.
main_findings: Biopsy C4d immunoreactivity was associated with subsequent cardiac allograft vasculopathy and death; autopsy findings were used in the outcome assessment of a deceased subset.
limitations: Abstract-only review. PDF pages 1 and extracted text visually checked on 2026-10-07.

Association is not causation. C4d/CAV, AMR and ACR are distinct targets; no biopsy/autopsy AI benefit or retrospective correction of an earlier ACR label is established. Abstract-only review; no current guideline recommendation is inferred.
does_not_establish: Association is not causation. C4d/CAV, AMR and ACR are distinct targets; no biopsy/autopsy AI benefit or retrospective correction of an earlier ACR label is established. Abstract-only review; no current guideline recommendation is inferred.
relevance_to_project: A heart-transplant precedent for linking biopsy marker information to later autopsy pathology rather than treating the two specimen types as interchangeable.
